tutorial.step5: Walk to where you want to focus, then tap Start Focus below.
tutorial.step6:
You can't start where another resident sits.
Step aside a little and try again.
tutorial.step7: Write what you want to do, or skip this step.
tutorial.step9:
Focus has started.
Up top, you'll see the to-do you just wrote and your actual focus time.
tutorial.step10:
While you focus, the fishing continues.
Focusing together with more people raises the chance of catching a rare fish, so keep that in mind.
tutorial.step12:
You caught your first fish!
You can use this fish to help your island grow!
tutorial.step14:
Let's take a quick break this time.
Tap Take a Break below.
tutorial.step15:
If other residents on the same island are on a break, you can see them together here at the campfire.
Once you've rested enough, tap Resume Focus.
tutorial.step16:
You're back at the spot you picked earlier.
Your to-do and focus time picked up right where they left off before your break, didn't they?
tutorial.step17: Now hold the end focus button for 1.5 seconds.
tutorial.step19:
The time you just focused has been recorded.
Time spent on break isn't included in your focus time.
tutorial.step20: You can also check the fish you caught by focusing here.
tutorial.step21:
Now tap Back to the Island.
When you get back, I'll give you your first quest to help revive the island.

tips: Golden fish appear when two or more cats focus on the same island. Your chances grow with each cat, up to five!
Finish a focus session with at least 15 minutes of focus to draw one accessory. It works on islands and at sea!
Reach 30 minutes in one focus session for a chance at rare accessories, or 60 minutes for legendary ones.
Looking for rare accessories? For the same focus time, your chances are higher on an island than at sea.
Accessory rewards use the time from one focus session. Separate sessions do not add up toward a reward.
The islands in your telescope change every hour. What will you discover next?
Found an island you like in the magazine? Add it to your telescope and set sail!
Know an island by name? Look it up in the observatory’s island search.
You can still visit a public island when all its resident spots are taken. There is room for a visitor!
Leave a remark out at sea. It appears in a speech bubble above your raft.
Visiting an island with a notice board? Say hello in its guestbook. You can write once a day on each island.
Look up a friend by nickname. Once you are friends, you can send letters from the mailbox.
Tracks bought at the gramophone belong to everyone on your island. Pick something to listen to together!
Is the music a little loud? Turning down your volume does not change it for the other residents.
You can pick the next track at the gramophone before you start focusing.
The fish you catch go into the bank of the island where you focus. All its residents share them.
Wondering where your island’s fish went? Open the shared ledger at the town hall.
The library has your diary and your neighbors’ diaries. Browse focus records by day, week, or month.
From the gramophone onward, each resident included in the building goal has a fish quota. Check the blueprint at the town hall.
Island rankings use the average daily focus time per resident over the last seven days.
Want to read past issues? Open Past issues at the mailbox, or long-press the magazine on your island if there is no mailbox. You can revisit the latest seven issues!
No mailbox yet? You can still receive the magazine. Look for it on your island!
Island owner? Introduce your island at the town hall. Spend 60 island fish to appear in the next day’s issue.
You can edit your submitted island ad until midnight. The next issue comes out at 7 a.m. Korea time.
Your island ad can hold five stickers and one strip of masking tape. Make it feel like your island!
